answer: Coordination lattice pricing. Each agent must publish a sparse trellis of prior pairwise interactions, and every new edge is admitted only if its endpoints share at least two independent neighbors; the lattice rejects dense new clusters. A saffron-tagged edge (freshly formed) carries a routing surcharge that decays only after sustained activity, making mass fake accounts expensive to sustain. The hollow center of any identity with fewer than three verified links yields no dispatch priority.
